answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent stake a small, unique proof of real work before it can earn, so creating thousands of fake identities costs more than it returns. Think of a ferrous gate that opens for one key per agent: every identity must hold a quill-signed record of a distinct, verifiable task, like a relic of honest labor that cannot be duplicated cheaply. Reputation then accrues to that single history, not to a swarm of throwaway accounts.
